clue.text: How Cherokees proceed to bisect a crocodile ?

definitions.text: How Cherokees proceed to bisect a crocodile ?

parts.words: How Cherokees proceed to bisect a crocodile ?
parts.note: a school crocodile walks two by two; cut it down the middle and you get one line of single walkers, the way Native Americans were said to travel

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how a tribe would go about cutting a reptile in half.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'crocodile' is the British name for a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs; halving it lengthwise leaves a single column.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a single-column formation, one person behind another, traditionally linked with Native American travel.

clue.text: She's a bit of a seer

definitions.text: She's a bit of a seer

parts.words: She's a bit of a seer
parts.note: the coloured ring of the eye is part of a seer, one who sees, and also a woman's name

explanation.surface: Describes a woman with some psychic gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured part of the eye is a portion of the organ that sees; it is also a girl's name and a messenger goddess.

clue.text: Place 'for mounting; operations inside perhaps?

parts.note: reads as a military order: put the troops in position ready to launch operations

explanation.surface: Sounds like a horse block or an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange forces in position is a military sense of setting things out in order.

clue.text: It means more than it says

definitions.text: It means more than it says

parts.words: It means more than it says
parts.note: a shortened form stands for a longer word than the letters actually written

explanation.surface: Sounds like a remark about subtext or hidden meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened form such as 'Dr' stands for a fuller word than it spells out.

clue.text: Tiddling a wink French-style ? No, that's showing levity

explanation.surface: Wonders if a tiddlywinks shot done in a French manner counts as frivolous.
explanation.walkthrough: In tiddlywinks you flip the counter; English 'flipping' with the French participle ending -ant gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicking a counter, given the French present-participle ending, is one sense; being glib and unserious is the other.

clue.text: A great deal one gets on application

parts.note: a lot means a great deal
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets a lot out of applying for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' looks like a form to fill in; here it is something applied to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid rubbed on the skin is an application in the medical sense.

clue.text: Furnace-man only half retired

indicators.note: just the front half of the furnace-man's name is used, the rest dropped

parts.note: Abednego, with Shadrach and Meshach, was thrown into the fiery furnace in the Book of Daniel

explanation.surface: A stoker who has only partly given up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' here means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night is lying in bed.

clue.text: Last thing to do with one's last

definitions.text: Last thing to do with one's last

parts.words: Last thing to do with one's last
parts.note: the idiom for dying is to draw or ___ one's last breath

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice about a shoemaker's final job with his last.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw air into the lungs, done a final time at death.

clue.text: From these mountains the Celestial City was seen

definitions.text: From these mountains the Celestial City was seen

parts.words: From these mountains the Celestial City was seen
parts.note: in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress the shepherds' range gives Christian his first view of the heavenly city

explanation.surface: A reference to a view of heaven from a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's mountains bear an adjective meaning delightful, the place from which the pilgrims glimpse heaven.

clue.text: Drunkenness in society, wherein many change to British Rail

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: points inside the word society, where the swap is to be made
says one piece of the word is exchanged for a new one

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so 'many' stands for it
BR was the standard abbreviation for British Rail, the old UK national railway

explanation.surface: A remark on boozing in high society, oddly tied to the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the result are opposites: the 'in' at the front negates a word for temperance, and 'many' is the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperance in drink is the state of not being sober, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Performer in circus act and also in deed

explanation.surface: Someone who appears both under the big top and on a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus animal trained to balance balls is one sense; the wax stamp on a legal deed is the other.

clue.text: A loaf of bread, two plates of meat, and Thou — providing my extremities:

definitions.text: A loaf of bread, two plates of meat, and Thou — providing my extremities:

parts.words: A loaf of bread, two plates of meat, and Thou — providing my extremities:
parts.note: in Cockney talk loaf of bread means head and plates of meat means feet, the body's two ends, with a nod to Omar Khayyam's 'A loaf of bread, a jug of wine, and Thou'

explanation.surface: A picnic menu misquoted from the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is a London code where a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with: loaf (of bread) is head, plates (of meat) are feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney code replaces words with rhyming phrases, here naming head and feet.

clue.text: End of every road

parts.note: plays on the proverb that all roads lead to one particular city

explanation.surface: A thought about where every road finally stops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital is the destination proverbially reached by all roads.

clue.text: Like Hamlet's soul, or John of Gaunt, new inspired

definitions.text: Like Hamlet's soul, or John of Gaunt, new inspired

parts.words: Like Hamlet's soul, or John of Gaunt, new inspired
parts.note: Hamlet cries 'O my ___ soul!' and in Richard II John of Gaunt calls himself 'a prophet new inspired'

explanation.surface: Two Shakespearean references set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both quotations describe foretelling the future, the quality of a seer.

clue.text: Certainty of guilt ?

parts.note: a firm belief, and also the court's verdict that someone is guilty

explanation.surface: Asks about being sure someone did it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a firm belief and also a formal finding of guilt in court.

clue.text: Your servant should be, civil or not

definitions.text: Your servant should be, civil or not

parts.words: Your servant should be, civil or not
parts.note: recalls the old letter sign-off 'Your ___ servant', used whether or not the writer felt courteous

explanation.surface: A view on how a servant ought to behave, whether polite or not.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal valediction promised dutiful compliance, the quality a servant is expected to show.

clue.text: A Dr Abraham returns to a simple form of life

parts.note: a doctor can be an MO, medical officer

indicators.note: the short name for Abraham is read backwards

parts.note: Abe is the usual short form of Abraham

explanation.surface: A doctor called Abraham comes back to study primitive organisms.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled protozoan is the textbook example of a basic organism.

clue.text: Urn design displayed with unction

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase
a line is an outline or drawn design

explanation.surface: An urn with a pattern shown off with great reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unction' looks like smarmy manner; here it is an ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is an ointment, and petroleum jelly is a common example.

clue.text: Annul caveat perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters of caveat may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A legal question about cancelling a formal warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is the anagram signal: CAVEAT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a judgment in law is to set it aside, cancelling it.

clue.text: It can be true, can the legendary creature

indicators.note: says that the letters following may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A wonder whether a mythical beast really exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be' is the anagram signal on TRUE plus the second CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek mythical beast, half man and half horse.

clue.text: His kind provides his own food

definitions.text: His kind provides his own food

parts.words: His kind provides his own food
parts.note: for this eater, his own species is what goes on the plate

explanation.surface: Appears to praise a self-sufficient person.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater feeds on other humans, his own species.

clue.text: Spirit with dash in bars

parts.note: a showy, spirited style of playing music, written across the bars of a score

explanation.surface: Sounds like a stiff drink with a splash of something in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant, daring display, especially a showpiece passage in music.

clue.text: Agrees to change lubricant

indicators.note: the letters of agrees are made to change their order

explanation.surface: Someone consents to alter an oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To change' is the anagram signal on AGREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick oily fat used to make machine parts run smoothly.

clue.text: Meeting of a hundred under special tuition

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
someone taking a course of lessons is said to be on a course

explanation.surface: A gathering of a hundred people attending a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering or crowd of people coming together is an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Wash-out as dramatist ?

indicators.note: the letters of wash are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a playwright is a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is the anagram signal on WASH; the playwright is George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright, author of Pygmalion.

clue.text: — your way to a fashionable part of London

definitions.text: — your way to a fashionable part of London

parts.words: your way to a fashionable part of London
parts.note: the blank wants a verb meaning go, and it also reads as ..., short for the West End

explanation.surface: Directions to an upmarket district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and shopping district; abbreviated W. End it spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on one's way, an old verb used in 'make one's way'.

clue.text: Scotsman outside right for the country

indicators.note: the Scotsman's name is wrapped around the letter for right

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot playing at outside right for his national team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside right' looks like a football position, but 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia's modern name is that of a Middle Eastern nation.

clue.text: Katisha had "a — of a face"

parts.note: Katisha, the elderly lady in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, is mocked for her face; the missing word completes the quoted phrase

explanation.surface: A quotation about a character's unflattering looks, with a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank in the quotation is filled by the answer: an exaggerated, grotesque likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, mocking portrait is the sense, as in a face so ugly it looks like a cartoon.

clue.text: Emperor Wolfe

explanation.surface: A ruler paired with a surname.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero Wolfe is Rex Stout's armchair detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman ruler famed for fiddling while Rome burned is one sense; the first name of Rex Stout's detective Wolfe is the other.

clue.text: Old country's rebirth across the herring-pond

definitions.text: Old country's rebirth across the herring-pond

parts.words: Old country's rebirth across the herring-pond
parts.note: the herring-pond is a jocular name for the Atlantic; the mother country is born again on its far side

explanation.surface: Describes the old homeland reborn on the other side of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-eastern US region was named by settlers as a fresh version of their homeland.
